title: XiangShan Kunminghu core, CONFIG=DefaultConfig (generated from Chisel) -- every module, sharded
_note: XiangShan (香山) is the open-source high-performance RISC-V processor from
the Institute of Computing Technology (Chinese Academy of Sciences) and the
Beijing Institute of Open Source Chip.  The core is written in Chisel/Scala:
the repository contains NO Verilog.  This family sweeps EVERY module of the
complete Kunminghu core (CONFIG=DefaultConfig: the configuration the chip
is built with), each with the exact parameterisation it has under XSTop --
firtool emits one concrete module per file, so a module IS its
instantiation and the per-module sweep is the per-instance sweep.
The generator does not fit a hosted runner (40 GB JVM heap, 3.2 M lines),
so the sweep fetches the generator's OUTPUT: the release asset
xiangshan-rtl-e4566c29 on alainmarcel/uhdm2rtlil holds build/rtl of
`make verilog CONFIG=DefaultConfig` at XiangShan e4566c29 (firtool
1.149.0), 2003 files.  To regenerate it locally use xiangshan-core-gen.json
(`make xiangshan-core-full-gen`).
max_closure_mb caps the source closure a module may pull in: Surelog needs
~0.25 GB per MB of this RTL, so 16 MB keeps two concurrent modules under the
runner's 12 GB cap.  1994 of the 2002 modules fit; XSTop, XSTile, XSCore,
Backend, CtrlBlock, MemBlock, Frontend and Rob are reported as skipped
(they are sweepable from a workstation with xiangshan-core-gen).
The hand-written SystemVerilog arithmetic library the same project ships
separately is swept as the "xiangshan" family (XS-Verilog-Library).
